title: SLI Hypothesis Lab and Priority Scorecard for Reliability Experiments
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable SLI hypothesis lab and a priority scorecard to track small-scale reliability experiments across product teams. The lab should standardize experiment definitions, measurement windows, and rollback criteria so PMs and Eng can run short SLI experiments (e.g., kv-cache eviction policy changes, small batching policy tweaks, canary kernel swaps) and report impact to error budgets and OKR traces. Deliverables: (1) SLI hypothesis template, (2) experiment scorecard with weighted priority and expected error-budget impact, (3) dashboard/Playbook links for running experiments, and (4) a short onboarding doc for PM/ENG experiment owners.
acceptance_criteria: Template: SLI hypothesis template exists in Confluence and includes success criteria, measurement windows, expected delta, and rollback plan
Scorecard: A spreadsheet and a Console view that ranks experiments by expected customer-impact, error-budget sensitivity, and implementation effort
Runbook: A 1-page experiment runbook with clear telemetry queries (Datadog/Prometheus) and SLI extraction instructions
Pilot: At least 3 pilot experiments run (two infra changes, one product change) with results logged and one iteration applied based on learnings
Visibility: Weekly digest added to Reliability Initiative Slack channel and automatic card creation in initiative tracker when an experiment starts
tasks: Draft SLI hypothesis template (PM + SRE) and link example for prefix-caching experiment
Design priority scorecard columns and weights (impact, error-budget risk, effort, auditability)
Prototype Console view: experiment list + status + estimated error-budget delta
Instrument 3 pilot experiments: ENG owners assigned and measurement queries defined
Write 1-page runbook and hosted Confluence doc; add template to new experiments folder
